# Shapes that must NOT be reported

Three shapes here look like the reported ones and are not. A report that
cannot tell them apart tells an author something untrue, which is worse than
saying nothing: the whole point of these messages is that an author can trust
them.

The document title carries the marker class. Metadata is not a placement site
at all — the marker machinery never reaches it — so nothing about it is
reported.

One term is marked here: [theta]{.index}.

A container holding a marker that HAS content is not left empty: the content is
spliced in where the marker stood, so the container still has something in it.

::: {#keeps-content .surrounding}
::: {.qi-index-here}
Content the marker kept, which leaves this container non-empty.
:::
:::

# The shape that places the index

The top-level marker below wraps a nested one. The outer marker is removed
whole — it places the index and reaches no output — so it is not a container
left empty by anything.

::: {.qi-index-here}
::: {.qi-index-here}
:::
:::

# The shape that IS reported

A footnote whose only content is a marker is emptied exactly as a div or a
block quote is, and is reported for the same reason.[^gone]

[^gone]:
    ::: {.qi-index-here}
    :::

# After the marker

Text after the marker, so the index's position is provable.
